record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.context_brief: Bounded slice indices with unbounded directional index
record.original_question: What conditions on the zero set and growth of an entire function F(z1,z2) provide both of the following properties: for every base point (z1^0,z2^0) in C^2, the one-variable slice t -> F(z1^0 + b1 t, z2^0 + b2 t) has bounded index, but the two-variable function F(z1,z2) has unbounded L-index in the direction b = (b1,b2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function and let $\mathbf{b}=(b_1,b_2)\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$ be a fixed direction. Let $L:\mathbb{C}^2\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function.

For each base point $(z_1^0,z_2^0)\in\mathbb{C}^2$, define the slice function
$$g_{(z_1^0,z_2^0)}(t)\;=\;F(z_1^0+b_1 t,\;z_2^0+b_2 t),\qquad t\in\mathbb{C}.$$
A one-variable entire function $g$ is said to have bounded index if there exists a non-negative integer $N$ such that for every $t\in\mathbb{C}$,
$$\max_{0\le k\le N}\frac{|g^{(k)}(t)|}{k!}\;\ge\;\frac{|g^{(n)}(t)|}{n!}\quad\text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$

The entire function $F$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists a non-negative integer $N$ such that for every $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb{C}^2$,
$$\max_{0\le k\le N}\frac{1}{k!\,L(z)^k}\Big|\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)\Big|\;\ge\;\frac{1}{n!\,L(z)^n}\Big|\partial^n_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)\Big|\quad\text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N}_0,$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}}F(z)=b_1\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_1}(z)+b_2\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_2}(z)$ and $\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}}F$ denotes the $k$-th iterate.

Find conditions on the zero set $F^{-1}(0)$ and on the growth of $F$ which together ensure both of the following simultaneously:

(i) for every base point $(z_1^0,z_2^0)\in\mathbb{C}^2$, the slice function $g_{(z_1^0,z_2^0)}(t)$ has bounded index (as a one-variable entire function);

(ii) the entire function $F$ does not have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ for the given $L$.
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
artifact.status_search_result: The problem belongs to a list of open problems on entire functions of bounded index in direction. Subsequent literature (work by Bandura, Skaskiv and collaborators in Matematychni Studii, MDPI Axioms, Ukrainian Mathematical Journal and Journal of Mathematical Sciences) develops criteria for boundedness of the L-index in direction (zero distribution, logarithmic derivative estimates, composition results), but no source located resolves this specific dichotomy of bounded slice indices coexisting with unbounded directional L-index. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Slice Holomorphic Functions in Several Variables with Bounded L-Index in Direction
status_evidence.snippet: Develops properties of slice holomorphic functions having bounded L-index in a direction; addresses related criteria but not the specific coexistence problem.
status_evidence.claim: The directional L-index theory is actively developed but the specified problem is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Some criteria of boundedness of the L-index in direction for slice holomorphic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes criteria of L-index boundedness in direction via zero distribution and logarithmic derivatives.
status_evidence.claim: Provides sufficient conditions for bounded L-index in direction but does not construct or characterize the requested 'bounded slice / unbounded directional' situation.
